exercise.name: Two-Arm Dumbbell Kickback
library_steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lean forward from your hips, back flat.
Keep your upper arms by your sides and straighten both arms back.
Bend your elbows slowly to return.
exercise.one_line_summary: Standing hip hinge ~60 deg with a flat back and soft knees; upper arms held just behind the body line, nearly level with the floor; elbows go from ~80 deg (forearms hanging vertical) to straight, palms facing in. Triceps does the work.

setup.target: Feet hip-width, knees soft, hinge at the hips until the torso is ~60 deg forward, back flat, head in line.
setup.tolerance: torso 45-75 deg from vertical; knee 15-35 deg
setup.why: ACE: torso stiff, head aligned, no low-back arching or rotation. Two-arm version has no hand on the thigh, so a moderate lean.

setup.target: Close to the torso, about parallel to it (elbows a little above the back line), and still.
setup.why: ACE: upper arm parallel and close to the torso, must not rise during the movement.

setup.target: Neutral grip, palms facing in; shoulder blades set down and back.

movement.measure: upper arm angle from the torso; plane -90 = straight behind

muscles.emg: Kickback 87 +- 27% of the triangle push-up, not significantly different from the best exercise (S1). Triceps EMG per unit force changes near full extension (120 deg) (S2) - the kickback is hardest at lockout.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Elbows drop to the hips at the start and lift at lockout.
mistakes.why_it_matters: ACE: the upper arm must not rise; the shoulder then does the work.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Hunched upper back or sagging low back during the hinge.
mistakes.why_it_matters: ACE: torso stiff, no low-back arching.

sources.citation: Boehler B, Porcari JP, Kline D, Hendrix CR, Foster C, Anders M. 2011. ACE-sponsored research: best triceps exercises. ACE Certified News, Aug 2011.
sources.what_it_gave: Kickback 87% of triangle push-up. Form: lean forward, torso stiff, head in line; upper arm parallel and close to the torso, stationary; elbow ~90 deg or forearm vertical; extend fully; scapula depressed and retracted.

sources.citation: Akima H, Maeda H, Koike T, Ishida K. 2021. Effect of elbow joint angles on electromyographic activity versus force relationships of synergistic muscles of the triceps brachii. PLoS ONE 16(6):e0252644.
sources.what_it_gave: Triceps heads at 60/90/120 deg elbow extension: heads alike; RMS-force relation shifts at the most extended angle.
